stem: Which statement best supports focusing preventive oral health care on higher-risk children?

options.text: Around 75% of caries are found in 25% of children
High caries rates in families are usually purely genetic
Poor saliva quality or flow is irrelevant if family history is absent
Prolonged night feeding lowers the risk of caries
Dental caries is too evenly distributed for targeted prevention to matter

explanation: Around 75% of caries are found in 25% of children. This shows that caries is concentrated in a smaller high-risk group, so prevention should be targeted rather than assuming an even distribution across all children.

citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes

optionExplanations.A: Correct because around 75% of caries are found in 25% of children, which supports a concentrated-risk pattern.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because family clustering of caries is not usually purely genetic and is more often influenced by environmental factors.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because poor saliva quality or flow is a recognised risk factor for caries.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because prolonged night feeding increases, rather than lowers, caries risk.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because caries burden is not evenly distributed across all children, so targeted prevention is useful.
